notes: Official page (newhorizonsforwomen.org.nz/education-awards.html) confirms this is a charitable trust grant programme (New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura) awarding small grants (NZD 1,000-3,000) to women at Certificate/Diploma/Degree level at any NZQA or Universities New Zealand approved tertiary institution. The award is not attached to any single institution, department, programme or supervisor; the Trust's own page lists no academic staff. No supervising professor exists to identify.

Official page (newhorizonsforwomen.org.nz/awards.html) confirms the Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund is a charitable trust project grant (up to NZD 4,000) for women-led peace initiatives, open to individuals enrolled at any tertiary institution, informal groups, or formal groups. Not attached to a specific institution or supervised programme; no academic faculty or supervisor is associated with the award.

Official page (ilsc.com/humanitarian-scholarship) confirms the ILSC Humanitarian Scholarship is a tuition-waiver scholarship for English language study (ELICOS) at a private language school chain (ILSC Australia campuses). It covers General English, exam preparation and EAP classes, with candidates selected by a committee of ILSC staff and teachers. No university attachment, no degree programme, and no supervising professors exist for this award.

Official notice (scholarships.gov.gh) confirms a bilateral Algeria/Ghana government scholarship administered by the Ghana Scholarships Authority, with study tenable in Algeria across broad disciplines (undergraduate, vocational/technical, Imam training, Master's in Islamic Studies). Applications go through the Ghana Scholarships Authority portal; no specific host institution, department or supervisor is named, so no professors can be tied to the award.

Official notice (scholarships.gov.gh) confirms a Kingdom of Saudi Arabia government scholarship allocation for Ghanaian citizens, applied for through the Saudi Ministry of Education's Study in Saudi platform (studyinsaudi.sa). Six participating universities are listed (Taif, Madinah, Jazan, Najran, Tabuk, Fahad Bin Sultan) but the award is a central government allocation across many fields with no specific programme, department or named supervisor; per guidance for national/government schemes with no attached institution, outcome is not_applicable.

The Heydar Aliyev International Education Grant is a central government grant programme of the Ministry of Science and Education of the Republic of Azerbaijan under the Study in Azerbaijan project. The official ministry page (edu.gov.az/en/programmes/study-in-azerbaijan-layihesi) returned a transport error on direct fetch from this environment, but its content was confirmed via search engine results of the exact URL: it describes the government grant (100 grants annually, established by presidential decree of 8 July 2023) with applicants applying through government authorities and the centralized SIACAS admission service to choose specialties across Azerbaijani higher education institutions. No single institution, department or supervisor is attached to the award, so no professors can be identified; analogous to MEXT/GKS-type central schemes.

Official service page (portal.gov.gy/services/scholarship, administered via mps.gov.gy/scholarships) confirms the Government of Guyana Scholarships are a national government scheme advertised individually by the Ministry of Public Service, Government Efficiency and Implementation across undergraduate, technical/vocational and postgraduate categories. Each award is advertised separately with its own requirements and host institution is determined per award; the scheme itself has no attached institution, programme or supervising professor.
